title: You're one of 74 soldiers about to destroy a bridge... by walking.
formula: Hook -> setting -> escalation -> snap -> deadpan double -> analogy -> consequence -> callback twist
facts: 12 April 1831, Broughton Suspension Bridge over the River Irwell, Salford near Manchester; opened 1826.
Suspension bridges were then called the 'new wonder of the age'; the bridge was a source of local pride.
A detachment of 74 men of the 60th Rifle Corps, returning to barracks from exercises on Kersal Moor, marching four abreast.
They felt it vibrate in time with their steps, found it amusing, whistled a marching tune and stepped to 'humour it'.
Near the far side they heard a sound like an irregular discharge of firearms; an iron column fell and the corner dropped 16-18 ft into the river.
About 40 men thrown into water about 2 ft deep; no deaths; 20 injured.
Investigation: a single badly forged bolt in a stay chain snapped; the bridge would likely have failed eventually anyway.
Result: the British Army ordered troops to break step when crossing bridges; 'break step' signs still exist (e.g. Albert Bridge, London).

lines.narration: You're one of 74 soldiers about to destroy a bridge... by *walking*.
lines.scene: Cold open: the bridge deck mid-bounce, bent like a wave, 74 stickmen in red coats stepping in perfect sync.
lines.gag: The bridge is visibly wobbling like jelly
lines.spoken: You're one of seventy-four soldiers about to destroy a bridge... by walking.

lines.narration: It's 1831, near Manchester, suspension bridges are the new wonder of the age, and this one is the town's *pride*.
lines.scene: Golden afternoon over the river; locals in top hats admire the chain bridge; a tiny sign: BROUGHTON BRIDGE.
lines.camera: Crane down from sky to the bridge
lines.spoken: It's eighteen thirty-one, near Manchester, suspension bridges are the new wonder of the age, and this one is the town's pride.

lines.narration: You're in the 60th Rifles, marching home from drills, four abreast. Left. Right. Left. *Right*.
lines.scene: Column of soldiers reaches the bridge; you in the front row, rust trim on your uniform.
lines.gag: Boots hit the deck with comic weight
lines.spoken: You're in the Sixtieth Rifles, marching home from drills, four abreast. Left. Right. Left. Right.

lines.narration: Halfway across, the bridge starts bouncing in time with your *feet*.
lines.scene: The deck rises and falls under each step; your hat bobs.
lines.camera: Side view, camera bobs with the deck
lines.gag: Everyone bobs in unison like a music video

lines.narration: A normal person would stop walking. 74 soldiers think it's *hilarious*.
lines.scene: Soldiers grinning at each other mid-bounce.
lines.spoken: A normal person would stop walking. [deadpan] Seventy-four soldiers think it's hilarious.

lines.narration: So some of you start whistling a marching tune... and stomp along on *purpose*.
lines.scene: Two soldiers whistle (music-note cards); everyone stomps harder.
lines.gag: Music notes bounce on the beat

lines.narration: The bridge bounces higher, and higher, it's basically a trampoline with a *river* under it!
lines.scene: Soldiers bounce into the air in sync, coat tails flying.
lines.camera: Tilt up following a soldier into the sky
lines.spoken: The bridge bounces higher, and HIGHER, it's basically a trampoline with a river under it!

lines.narration: Wait... why does it sound like someone's firing *guns*?
lines.scene: Smiles freeze; little crack lines spark at the far pier.
lines.camera: Punch close-up on your face, hard cut

lines.narration: An iron column snaps, and the whole corner drops 16 feet into the *river*.
lines.scene: The column topples (cut away before impact); the deck corner swings down; splash wall.
lines.camera: Impact kick, fast tilt down with the fall
lines.spoken: An iron column snaps, and the whole corner drops sixteen feet into the river.

lines.narration: Luckily, the river is only 2 feet *deep*.
lines.scene: You standing in the river, water at your knees, hat floating.
lines.gag: You look down at the tiny water level, relieved
lines.spoken: Luckily, the river is only two feet deep.

lines.narration: Unluckily, the river is only 2 feet *deep*.
lines.scene: Same shot; a second soldier lands next to you, bum first. Ow-stars.
lines.spoken: Unluckily... the river is only two feet deep.

lines.narration: About 40 of you go in, 20 get hurt, and incredibly, nobody *dies*.
lines.scene: Soldiers sitting in the shallow river, bandaged, a few with arm slings; townsfolk rushing to help.
lines.gag: One townsman brings a single towel for forty men
lines.spoken: About forty of you go in, twenty get hurt, and incredibly, nobody dies.

lines.narration: You see, a bridge bounces like a kid on a *swing*.
lines.scene: Analogy card world: you push a kid on a swing; the swing arcs bigger each push.
lines.gag: The kid on the swing is a tiny bridge with a face

lines.narration: Push at just the right moment, every time, and it goes higher... and *higher*.
lines.scene: You push the swing; each arc is bigger.
lines.camera: Follow the swing up, tilt to sky
lines.gag: Swing loops all the way over the top
lines.spoken: Push at just the right moment, every time, and it goes higher... and HIGHER.

lines.narration: 74 pairs of boots in perfect rhythm? That's the best-timed push a bridge has ever *felt*.
lines.scene: Swing replaced by the bridge, the column of boots as the 'push'.
lines.camera: Match cut from swing to bridge
lines.spoken: Seventy-four pairs of boots in perfect rhythm? That's the best-timed push a bridge has ever felt.

lines.narration: To be fair, investigators found one badly made bolt that would have failed *eventually*. You just made 'eventually' happen *early*.
lines.scene: Investigator with a magnifying glass on a tiny cracked bolt; it gives a sad shrug.

lines.narration: So the British Army made a new rule: soldiers must break step when crossing a *bridge*.
lines.scene: Officer nailing up a sign: 'TROOPS MUST BREAK STEP'.
lines.camera: Low angle push on the sign
lines.gag: The officer's hammer strokes make the sign bounce

lines.narration: Nearly 200 years later, some bridges still carry that *sign*.
lines.scene: Same sign, now old and weathered, on a modern bridge with traffic.
lines.gag: A jogger in headphones crosses perfectly in rhythm; the sign shakes
lines.spoken: Nearly two hundred years later, some bridges still carry that sign.

lines.narration: Because the one thing an army can never do on a bridge... is *march*.
lines.scene: Back to the cold-open bridge in sync; you mid-step, look at camera.
lines.camera: Push-in on you, end on the word
